Can we understand a bit better who’s being blamed here? The original article blamed “systematic funds” or trend-following strategies, which is honestly some of the oldest and tiresome excuses for market volatility that I just don’t believe to be true. 

And then all the replies and quotes seem to have moved onto the “incentive structures at these funds”. A systematic trend-following strategy has no incentives structure. It’s fully systematic and non-discretionary at inception. 

What they seem to be alluding at is the incentive structure at the multistrat discretionary equity pods with tight risk budgets that offer almost a real call option. Do pods have an incentive to crowd into the same momentum trades. Well I guess I can see that esp during a bubble. But someone should document it. 

What I don’t know is if pods are any likelier to be crowded into the same momentum trades and rush for the exit causing large market drawdowns. See the behaviors of HFs documented during the DotCom Bubble, before multistrats were even popular. It was the same exact thing. 

In fact, if anything we should celebrate and marvel at the fact that despite the proliferation of systematic strategies and crowded trades at the pods what not, volatility at the aggregate market level remains historically low despite the extraordinary bull run. VIX or volatility on SPX, where most of the money sits is well below the levels reached in the late 90s and 2000s even with the gyrations and degen meme trades extra. 

If this isn’t market efficiency I don’t know what is.

It think it's stupid that "AI Bubble" gets used over and over. In infra names you have: 

- 1-3x fwd P/E memory companies from Samsung to $ESMT. With HBM players now having hyperscaler multi-year price floor LTAs. 

- Optical companies like $POET traded -$97M under net cash. Valuing the operating business very negatively, not even at $0. 

- While AI companies with larger premiums continue to record demand over the next 3-5 years. Such as the new $20B LTAs signed w/ $COHR to $5B LTAs signed w/ $LITE. 

Can someone in the media honestly see negative EV high-beta optical companies, where 2 years of burnrate would still value the company below $0.  

or single digit memory companies with contracted demand + price floors years out and say that's a bubble?

Many of these names are extremely profitable today... 

But obviously there's other elements inside the theme, such as: 

- Certain startups like Instinct that look like a private valuation bubble. 
- Leveraged Neoclouds that didn't finance properly
- and AI lab valuations and commitments, which should be viewed cautiously. 

But everything gets grouped into one with the boogyman of "leverage" or "debt". 

Yes, valuations can compress or correct from macro, potential regulatory uncertainty, or potential capex reductions. 

But for the companies physically powering the AI buildout, it looks more like the Great AI Deleveraging of 2026... 

Than anything like fundamental demand destruction.

As more earnings come out and free cash flow accumulates over time.

I'm confident in a recovery, especially in bottlenecks, and for markets to eventually discern durability + growth over frothy valuations tied to AI.

correct, this is the stablecoin trilemma (made up term, dont think anyone ever wrote this down):

between three properties of 
1) crypto-backed/immutable
2) solvent
3) scalable,
a stablecoin can only choose 2 of 3. 

old-dai, lusd chose 1+2 (sacrifice scalability)
usdt, usdc choose 2+3 (sacrifice immutability)
terrausd and its many clones chose 1+3 (sacrifice solvency)

note that the three choices not equal: 
- a stablecoin that isnt solvent fails its single most important test.
- give that money's utility scales with its network, sacrificing scalability is a large price that ultimately dooms the coin to failure
- immutability, then, is arguably the least-bad thing to sacrifice, because ("the only free lunch") it can be at least partially addressed with diversification. you also become less vulnerable with scale (see tether being a huge holder of t-bills giving it a certain political immunity)

now that apple put xcode inside claude code, here’s how i’d find, build and grow an iOS app with AI agents:

find it
- open appfigures or sensor tower and sort utilities by revenue
- filter for apps with a rating under 3.5
- bonus points if the top app hasn't shipped an update in 6+ months
- check the keywords they rank for in appfigures. low difficulty + high revenue is the sweet spot
- scroll the "you might also like" row on the top app's page. every app there is another market to check
- or find a startup idea on https://t.co/a5ARFnvky2 based on social sentiment

validate it
- use facundoolano/app-store-scraper to pull every review for the top 20
- give them to an agent: "cluster the 1 and 2 star reviews into the top 5 complaints and quote the users"
- pick the app where the complaints are about the product, not the price
- if people complain about the price but keep paying, that's demand. if they complain about bugs, that's your opening
- search reddit for "alternative to [app]". every thread is a list of people waiting for you

build it
- claude code + apple's new xcode plugin to build, preview and fix
- cameroncooke/XcodeBuildMCP so the agent can build, test and run the simulator on its own
- joshuayoes/ios-simulator-mcp so it can tap, swipe and screenshot like a user
- write a skill with the top 5 complaints so every feature gets checked against them
- apple's foundation models for on-device ai, so your inference cost is $0
- app intents so siri and personal agents can use your app too
- add an "import from [competitor]" button. make switching take 10 seconds

test it
- maestro tests every flow the reviewers complained about
- the agent runs them on every screen size before each build
- if the competitor's worst flow takes 6 taps, yours takes 2
- sentry for crashes, telemetrydeck for analytics
- testflight it to 20 people from those reddit threads before launch

monetize it
- revenuecat for subscriptions and mrr
- superwall to test paywalls without shipping a new build
- paywall right after the first win, never on launch
- annual as the default with a 3-day trial, weekly as the anchor
- turn on win-back offers for everyone who cancels

rank it
- your screenshots answer each complaint directly. "no ads." "works offline." "cancel anytime."
- fastlane snapshot + frameit regenerates every screenshot automatically
- a/b test them with app store connect's product page optimization
- have the agent localize your listing into 10 languages. most competitors only rank in english
- ask for a review right after a win with apple's built-in review prompt, never after an error

grow it
- find 10 creators in your niche on tiktok one. small monthly base + a bonus for every 100k views
- give each one a fresh tiktok account that only posts about your niche
- apify's tiktok scraper pulls the top 100 hooks in your niche every week. that's your hook bank
- every creator tests 3 new hooks a day in capcut. anything that loses people in the first 3 seconds gets cut
- arcads or heygen for ai ugc when you need 50 variations of a winner
- postiz to schedule everything across tiktok, reels and shorts
- faceless slideshow accounts posting 3x a day: problem, screenshot, result
- when an organic video takes off, put money behind it with tiktok spark ads instead of making new ads
- a unique apple offer code for every creator so you know exactly who drove each subscriber
- a quiz landing page on framer that ends in "download the app." web-to-app funnels convert better than cold traffic
- appsflyer to track which video, creator and ad actually turned into revenue
- apple ads on the competitor's name

i could do a whole episode on @startupideaspod if people are interested. i will never gatekeep anything im learning in real-time.

welcome to the golden age of ios apps, because now anyone can build one

Highly recommend :)
